summary.text: Zellnor Myrie is the incumbent Democratic and Working Families Party state senator for District 20 in Brooklyn. A Brooklyn native and attorney, he worked as a City Council legislative director and at Davis Polk & Wardwell before defeating incumbent Jesse Hamilton in 2018. He chairs the Senate Codes Committee, ran unsuccessfully for New York City Mayor in 2025, and is the only candidate listed on the November 3, 2026 ballot for the seat.

paragraphs.text: Zellnor Myrie was born in Brooklyn on November 3, 1986, to Costa Rican-born immigrant parents and was raised in Prospect Lefferts Gardens; his official biography says his mother moved to Brooklyn from Costa Rica and is an inspiration for his public service.

He graduated from Brooklyn Technical High School, earned a B.A. in Communications and an M.A. in Urban Studies from Fordham University, and received a J.D. from Cornell Law School, where he served as student government president.
Before law school he worked as legislative director to New York City Council Member Fernando Cabrera, and after law school he spent just over a year at the law firm Davis Polk & Wardwell.
Myrie left the firm to run for the State Senate in 2018, defeating incumbent Jesse Hamilton in the Democratic primary and again in the general election, and he took office on January 1, 2019.

In the 2025-2026 session he chairs the Senate Codes Committee and is also a member of the Children and Families, Consumer Protection, Elections, Health, Judiciary, and Rules committees; his official biography says he previously chaired the Elections Committee.

According to that biography, his legislative work includes tenant protection and criminal-legal-system measures, a 2021 state law on gun industry liability, election measures including early voting, and authorship of the John R. Lewis New York Voting Rights Act.
Myrie ran for New York City Mayor in 2025 and placed sixth in the first round of the Democratic primary; the winner of that primary, Zohran Mamdani, went on to win the general election.
